advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a function-level opt-out marker should exempt file-scoped (module-level-helper) hazards, or only a true module `pytestmark`; scope `exempt_files` accordingly and add a test.
evidence: `self.exempt_functions.setdefault(path, set()).add(name)` immediately followed by `self.exempt_files.add(path)` in `absorb` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:457-458) — the file-level exemption is set for ANY marker, not only a module `pytestmark`.

`fails` non-test branch: `return path not in self.exempt_files` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:475) — a module-level-helper hazard is excused whenever any collected item in the file carried the marker.

The docstring at tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:472-474 claims a helper is covered by "a file-level opt-out (typically a module `pytestmark`)", but the code makes a per-function marker equally file-scoping.

ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py references `exempt_files` or covers a function-marked test coexisting with an unmarked test that reaches a module-level-helper hazard.
advisory.finding: A single FUNCTION-level `@pytest.mark.allow_unharnessed_subprocess` marker adds the file path to `exempt_files`, which then exempts ALL module-level-helper (non-test) hazards in that file — including helpers exercised by OTHER, unmarked tests. The opt-out for one test silently excuses file-scoped hazards it never intended to cover.
scenarios: A file has one test marked allow_unharnessed_subprocess plus an unmarked test that calls a module-level helper which spawns a hazardous unharnessed subprocess — the helper's hazard is silently exempted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align `_PREFILTER_TOKENS` with the resolver so `from os import system/popen` (and any aliased subprocess import) still triggers a parse, or drop the byte prefilter for the `os` callees.
evidence: `_PREFILTER_TOKENS = (b"subprocess", b"os.system", b"os.popen", b"pytest.main")` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:59).

`_import_bindings` records `functions[alias.asname or alias.name] = f"{node.module}.{alias.name}"` for ImportFrom (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:81-83), so `from os import system` binds `system` -> `os.system`, which is in `_SPAWN_TARGETS`.

`scan_path` only parses when `_might_spawn(raw)` is true: `findings = scan_source(...) if _might_spawn(raw) else []` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:402) — a file using `from os import system` (source never contains the byte string `os.system`) is skipped.
ABSENCE: `search_files 'from os import'` under tests/unit returns no matches today, so no live regression — but the gap is latent and fail-open on introduction of such an import.
advisory.finding: The byte pre-filter `_PREFILTER_TOKENS` and the AST callee resolver disagree for `os.system`/`os.popen` imported via `from os import system`/`from os import popen`: such a call is a resolvable spawn callee the scanner would classify as a hazard, but the `b"os.system"`/`b"os.popen"` byte tokens never appear in that import style, so `_might_spawn` returns False, the file is skipped unparsed, and the hazard is invisible.
scenarios: A future unit test does `from os import system` (or `popen`) and calls `system(...)` rooted at the checkout — the guard silently skips the file.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add bare `b"import system"`/`b"popen"` insufficient — instead include `b"import"`-agnostic tokens such as `b" system"`/`b" popen"` cautiously, or simply parse any file that contains `b"os"`+`b"system"`; safest is to widen tokens to `b"system"` and `b"popen"`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider detecting checkout-rooted cwd expressions beyond the REPO_ROOT/_REPO_ROOT name whitelist (e.g. `Path(__file__)...parents[n]`), or document the residual gap explicitly in the guard's contract.
evidence: `if _mentions(explicit, harness) or not _mentions(explicit, _REPO_ROOT_NAMES): return` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:287) — a cwd not mentioning REPO_ROOT/_REPO_ROOT is treated as clean.
`_REPO_ROOT_NAMES = frozenset({"REPO_ROOT", "_REPO_ROOT"})` (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:52).
The module docstring (tests/_subprocess_isolation.py:24-27) frames the three-way classification as a deliberate tradeoff, so this is a documented heuristic boundary rather than an oversight.
advisory.finding: `_check_root` recognizes a checkout-rooted cwd only when the expression textually mentions the names REPO_ROOT/_REPO_ROOT; a spawn with `cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` (the real checkout computed inline) is neither harness-owned nor name-matched, so it passes as clean.
scenarios: A test computes the checkout root inline (e.g. `parents[2]`) and passes it as cwd without binding it to a REPO_ROOT-named constant.

advisory.finding: The oracle never exercises the `from subprocess import run` bare-name resolution path — the core `function_aliases` half of `_import_bindings`. A module writing `from subprocess import run` then `run([...], cwd=REPO_ROOT)` should be flagged a hazard, but no test drives it; a mutant deleting the `ast.ImportFrom` branch of `_import_bindings` (functions[...] = f"{node.module}.{alias.name}") survives the whole suite. `test_a_locally_defined_run_is_not_a_spawn` only asserts the NEGATIVE (an un-imported local `run` is ignored), so the positive from-import binding is regression-blind.
merged_from: The aliased-module resolution path (`import subprocess as sp` -> module_aliases['sp']='subprocess', then `sp.run(...)`) is untested. `_import_bindings` builds `modules[local] = alias.name` specifically for aliased imports and `_resolve_callee` rewrites `sp.run` to `subprocess.run`, but every oracle test uses the un-aliased name `subprocess`, so a regression collapsing module-alias handling would not be caught.

Four spawn targets declared in `_SPAWN_TARGETS` — `subprocess.check_output`, `subprocess.check_call`, `subprocess.call`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, `pytest.main` — are newly added detection surface but only `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.Popen` have detection tests. A mutant dropping any of the other entries from `_SPAWN_TARGETS` survives the suite.
scenarios: A refactor breaks ImportFrom binding resolution; real from-imported spawn sites silently stop being detected
